Education projects, documented

I'm Kieran Nolan, an educational technologist with 20+ years in classrooms. This is where I write up what actually happens when primary school kids get their hands on real networks, real servers, Minecraft, robotics, game development, VR and Bitcoin. Field notes, not theory. Articles get posted for discussion to Stacker News ~education, a territory managed by the Digital Playhouse Foundation, the charity I serve on the board of.

Red vs Blue: teaching cyber security to a whole primary school inside Minecraft

A six-week, whole-school program: 16 classes from Foundation to Year 6, two castles, two real Umbrel servers to defend, versioned builds approved by team consensus, and a final-day hunt for a hidden IP address.

The classroom with its own internet: running school infrastructure over Starlink

The Ancient City: a whole school builds in Minecraft, then prints it in 3D

Term 1 in the SPARK Centre: every student built one plot of an ancient city in Minecraft, exported it as a .mcstructure, converted it to STL and 3D printed it, then the prints came together as one city.
